overview: Retrospective segmented time series of recognition of known airway difficulty before later airway management, January 2019 to August 2026, using the difficult airway database linked to anaesthetic records and incident reports.
population: Patients registered in the difficult airway database who had a later airway management episode (anaesthetic or emergency intubation) in the hospital; the first later episode per patient per quarter is counted.
exposure: Airway management after 1 March 2023, when the wristband, electronic alert and letter were in place, compared with the pre-existing trend.
procedures: Two trainees review the anaesthetic record of each later episode using a tested form: whether the alert was present, whether known difficulty was documented as recognised before airway management, the airway plan, and whether difficulty was unanticipated. A random 15 percent are reviewed by both trainees. Database capture is checked against a manual review of one year's anaesthetic records. Co-interventions (training, equipment, guidelines) are listed with dates.

outcomes.name: Known difficulty recognised before airway management
outcomes.measure: Proportion of later airway management episodes with documented recognition of known difficulty beforehand, per quarter
outcomes.why: The mechanism the alert system exists to deliver.

outcomes.name: Unanticipated difficulty
outcomes.measure: Proportion of later episodes with difficulty not anticipated in the plan

outcomes.name: Alert present in the record
outcomes.measure: Proportion of later episodes with the electronic alert displayed
outcomes.why: Separates missing alerts from unread ones.

outcomes.name: Alert burden
outcomes.measure: Number of other electronic warnings displayed to the anaesthetist

feasibility: About 400 later episodes over the period; two trainees at two sessions a week can review them in about five months.
biasMitigation: Segmented regression with the pre-existing trend
Co-interventions listed with dates and modelled where possible
Double review of 15 percent of records

biasFlags.label: Co-interventions
biasFlags.note: Other airway initiatives started around the change.

biasFlags.label: Documentation of recognition
biasFlags.note: Recognition may happen without being written down.

parsimony.simplestPath: One series, one primary outcome, one change point.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the segmented time series structure.
summary: Segmented series with recognition as the primary outcome and database capture reported.
